correctness.rationale: Normalize: all distinct branch identifications are real, so the complex curve is the real graph with two disks attached along each normalization equator. Unibranch singular points do not impose further identifications. Thus the integral boundary graph quotient is exactly by the independent equators, which have disjoint edge supports. For the real pair, H2(RP2;Z)=0; relative H2 is freely generated by the orientable chambers and injects into graph H1 with image ker eta. Modulo 2, all chambers contribute and H2(RP2;F2) injects into relative H2 (the real locus is a graph). Comparing integral and mod-2 ranks gives exactly 1-epsilon nonorientable chambers. Parity of the degrees kills the equators under eta. On the complex side the degree map contributes the torsion Z/d and the boundary maps onto the free H1 of the graph quotient. For each real chain R_i bounding an equator, Z_i=R_i-H_i is an absolute cycle. Subtract its conjugate: (1-c*)[Z_i]=-[C_i]; since c* acts by -1 on the ambient generator, [Z_i]=-d_i/2 times that generator. Hence the image of the equator lattice in torsion is exactly the order-two subgroup, since the d_i/d have gcd 1. The boundary diagram gives the claimed parity kernel, free-boundary index 2^epsilon, and stated cokernel sequence and generation criterion. The two-conic examples have the reported epsilon values and indices 2 and 1, respectively. The supplied checker was read, not run; it checks abstract integer presentations, not this topological lemma. Ancillary wording erratum: SLOGAN.txt says 'Each normalization circle contributes the unique order-two torsion class'. In the theorem each contributes either zero or that class according to d_i/d, and together they generate it. RESULT.md states this correctly.
